Subject: Pricing exhibit - volume cushion and packaging mapping (redline attached)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our procurement team reviewed the order schedule and attached a redline (CloudCare_Redline_v3.docx) with a few changes focused on: the "volume cushion" definition in Exhibit B, the application of caps/floors during quarter-to-quarter true-ups, and how bundled SKUs map back to the fee bands (packaging mapping).

Two specific asks:
- Can you confirm whether the "volume cushion" is intended as a per-quarter buffer (i.e., applied before true-up) or an annual aggregated buffer? The redline proposes treating it per-quarter to avoid surprise invoicing, but that could materially change our fiscal treatment.
- We flagged a scenario where SKU bundles get reclassified between fee bands during migration periods. The redline asks that migration conversions use the average monthly run-rate across the quarter rather than a single day snapshot. Please confirm if Redwood can support that operationally.

I understand some of these items touch legal (caps/floors) and implementation (billing ops). Looping procurement as they'll own sign-off if legal accepts. If you can get a short legal interpretation and an ops confirmation by Friday (2026-11-27), we can move this to DocuSign the following week.

Attachments: CloudCare_Redline_v3.docx (edits in Exhibit B + Order Schedule)

Subject: RE: Pricing exhibit - volume cushion and packaging mapping (legal commentary attached)

Hi all — I reviewed the CloudCare redline and drafted proposed contract language and commentary (see attached Legal_Commentary_LB.pdf). Key points: 

- "Volume cushion" interpretation: the safest construct for both parties is to define the cushion as a per-invoice-period buffer (the quarter) with a cap on annual exposure. Suggested language: "Volume Cushion: For the avoidance of doubt, the Volume Cushion shall be applied per billing quarter for the purposes of calculating overage true-ups, provided that Redwood's aggregate annual billing exposure attributable to all Volume Cushions shall not exceed X% of the committed annual spend." This preserves CloudCare's ask for quarterly smoothing while protecting Redwood from unlimited leakage.

- Caps/Floors during true-up: The proposed redline sought to change the floor calculation to a "best-of" approach which materially reduces minimum revenue. As a compromise, I propose retaining the floor as drafted but adding a one-time grace adjustment for migration quarters where a reclassification materially alters band assignment by > 15%. Language included in the attachment.

- Packaging mapping / migration snapshot: I am comfortable with the quarter-average approach for reclassification, but recommend a timebox: apply averaging for the first two migration quarters only, after which standard snapshot rules resume. This avoids permanent ambiguity.

Operational caveats that Redwood should call out in contract: any averaging or migration exceptions will require a separate reconciliation run and a short manual approval step in billing ops. Karthik, please confirm the expected additional cycle time and whether this impacts invoice delivery timing.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Karthik to confirm ops timing and whether the reconciliation requires a billing window extension.
2) I will incorporate the drafted language directly into your CloudCare_Redline_v3.docx and return a tracked version.
3) If accepted, Stephanie to prepare final combined markup for DocuSign.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Regards,

- The per-quarter cushion with an annual exposure cap is acceptable. Please insert a numeric cap (we're ok with discussing X% in private, but can you provide Redwood's proposed cap range so procurement can finalize approval)?
- The two-quarter timebox for averaging during migration is reasonable. We'll accept the manual reconciliation step; please call out SLA for completing reconciliation so we can set expectations for invoicing cadence.

If you can return a tracked version of the order schedule with Laura's language and a short ops note from Karthik (billing cycle impact and SLA), we'll aim to finalize sign-off on 2026-11-27 and target DocuSign by 2026-11-30.
